$comment: Everything the fork changes relative to upstream. tools/fork/check-fork.mjs enforces this in CI and FORK.md explains it. Register a new hook here in the same commit that adds it.

touchpoints.purpose: A short banner at the top of upstream's README saying what this fork adds and pointing at FORK.md.
Passes upstream's config through withForkIdentity from fork.config.ts, so the fork has its own name and bundle ID and installs beside the official app.

One @import of podcasts/themes.css, which declares the Podcasts section's extra themes (Extra Dark, Midnight, Paper, Forest) as Uniwind variants. A block at the end gives the app's own light and dark themes Apple's colours (docs/BOOKS-APPLE-DESIGN.md); it sits at the end because Uniwind allows @import only at the top, where the upstream values would override it.

Puts the menu button at the top left of the Books screen. It opens the side menu with Books and Podcasts. The screen is also restyled with the Apple look (docs/BOOKS-APPLE-DESIGN.md): on iOS its list comes first and apple-look/BooksHomeBar.tsx draws the native bar with the side menu, Search and the home menu.
Lists the Podcasts section's extra theme names in extraThemes of withUniwindConfig, so Uniwind builds the colours declared in podcasts/themes.css.
Shows the atmosphere sounds' section (on and off, volume, how much is going on, the car, importing a sounds folder) under the reading settings.

Adds the atmosphere sounds button to the player's toolbar for readaloud books, in both the read-along and listening screens. The toolbar is also restyled with the Apple look (docs/BOOKS-APPLE-DESIGN.md): round buttons, a glass capsule in the reader, white icons over the player's cover wash.

Imports lofi/readerFollow.ts for its listeners, so the sounds follow the pages while the listener reads a readaloud book on screen with the narration stopped. Also imports modules/podcasts/background.ts, which defines the podcasts background task while the app starts (iOS may start the app in the background just to run it).

Lets the atmosphere pause the narration for a moment at a big scene change (the hold in LofiNarratorBridge.swift) without the app, the lock screen or the remote buttons seeing a pause, and ends that hold on pause, play or the sleep timer. Each of the eight lock-screen handlers also asks LofiRemoteHandoff.swift first, so a playing podcast owns the lock screen and headphone buttons. The book does not resume after a call or Siri while a podcast owns the lock screen (the podcast player resumes its own episode).
